_comment: Hand-maintained input to `pnpm identities`. The bootstrap merges clusters
sharing a normalised name by default (KSC is small enough that one name is
one sailor); this file records the cross-spelling merges the matcher cannot
see, and the exceptions to that default. See CLARIFICATIONS.md §9.
unify   - one sailor published under several spellings. `name` is the
display name; `aliases` are the other spellings as they appear.
separate- a name that really is two or more different sailors, so the
one-name-one-sailor default must not merge them.
rename  - fix a display name without changing which rows group together.
A merge is only listed here when the variants share a club, never appear in
the same series, and differ by an obvious slip - a doubled or dropped
letter, a transposition, Mac/Mc spacing, or a dropped O'. Pairs that fail
any of those tests are left apart and asked about instead: under-linking
splits one sailor's record, but over-linking puts another sailor's results
in it, which is the worse error and the harder one to notice.

unify.name: Andres Gonzalves
unify.note: One Fireball sailor, published under five spellings across 2019-2024 (all KSC, all Fireball). Confirmed by the club. The display name is the commonest of the five; the correct spelling is still to be confirmed.

unify.name: Barry O'Donovan
unify.note: One row each, same club recorded as 'KSC' and 'Killaloe Sailing Club'.

unify.name: Fionn McNamara
unify.note: Both Lough Ree, 2023 — unlike his namesake Siofra, whose two spellings carry different clubs and are left apart.

unify.name: Brian Keane
unify.note: A boat entered under two sailors' names in the helm field; attributed to the first named, as the matcher already did for the two Ryan rows it could resolve by sail number. The second sailor loses a row they arguably should keep — sailscoring#348 (crew identity) is the real fix.
